title: Four loans in one pool (toy, ours)
note: A pool of 4 loans worth 10 each. The junior tranche (20) takes the first losses. The senior tranche (20) loses money only if 3 or 4 loans default.

params.label: share of risk that is one common factor

readout: Chance the senior tranche loses money: {pmix:.3%}. With independent loans it would be {pind:.4%}; your mix is {ratio:.1f} times that.
caption: Toy, ours. With probability w all loans follow one shared coin; otherwise they are independent. Each loan always has default chance p. Idea from FCIC p. 149 (pooling assumed to diversify).

title: How many contracts have a short description? (toy, ours)
note: A contract pays 0–9 for each possible state of the village. Drag k: how many contracts can have a description shorter than k bits?
readout: {states:d} weather states, so 10^{states:d} contracts. Naming one takes {bits:.2f} bits. At most {nshort:,} contracts have a description shorter than {k:d} bits: a fraction {frac:.3g} of all (1 means all of them).
caption: Counting argument: Cover and Thomas 1991, Theorem 7.2.4, p. 150. Mapping contracts to bit strings is our step. Toy, ours.

title: Requisite variety for a supervisor (toy, ours)
note: Variety = log2 of the number of different situations (or responses). The supervisor sees contract types; each needs its own kind of check.

params.label: allowed contract types: 10 to the power

readout: V_D = {vd:.2f} bits, V_R = {vr:.1f} bits. Least outcome variety V_O ≥ {vo:.2f} bits.
caption: Ashby 1956, S.11/6–11/7, pp. 206–207: V_O cannot be less than V_D − V_R. Mapping to supervisors and contracts is our analogy. Toy, ours.

title: How many independent opinions? (toy, ours)
note: N forecasts, each pair correlated by rho. N_eff is the number of independent forecasts that would give an average as steady as yours.
readout: N_eff = {neff:.3f} of {N:d} banks. However many banks join, N_eff never exceeds 1/rho = {limit:.2f}. Each bank is wrong on 1% of days; all wrong together: {pall_ind:.2e} if independent, about {pall_one:.0%} if they run one model.
caption: Formula N_eff = N / (1 + (N − 1) rho): our derivation (variance of an average of equally correlated forecasts). Toy, ours.

title: Counting one signal many times (toy, ours)
note: Prior 1/2 that the bank is safe. A model says safe; a safe bank is 4 times as likely to get this verdict as a risky one. How many separate pieces of evidence do you really hold?
caption: Same arithmetic as post 01, world W4 (likelihood ratio 4). New story, ours. Odds form of Bayes: posterior odds = prior odds × LR^n.
